PORT ARMSTRONG TERMINAL HARVEST AREA TROLL FISHERY

The Port Armstrong Terminal Harvest Area (THA) commercial salmon troll fishery will open for the harvest of coho, chum, pink, and sockeye salmon from 12:01 a.m., Wednesday, July 1, through 11:59 p.m., Sunday, September 20, 2026, unless closed by emergency order. Chinook salmon may only be retained and possessed in the THA during open Chinook salmon retention periods established for the summer troll fishery under 5 AAC 29.100(c).

The waters of the Port Armstrong THA (statistical area 109-11) are described as the waters of Port Armstrong west of a line from Point Eliza at 56°17.70′ N lat, 134°38.89′ W long to a point on the Baranof Island shoreline at 56°17.97′ N lat, 134°38.44′ W long (Figure 1).

Waters north of a line from 56°17.61′ N lat, 134°40.27′ W long, to 56°17.67′ N lat, 134°39.64′ W long are closed to commercial salmon fishing with troll gear.

Figure 1.–Waters of the Port Armstrong THA open to troll gear.

Port Armstrong THA Troll Fishery

June 24, 2026

Port Armstrong THA Troll Fishery page 2 of 2

June 24, 2026

Trollers and processors are instructed to report statistical area 109-10 on fish tickets when documenting salmon harvested in the waters of Chatham Strait adjacent to the Port Armstrong THA.

The Emergency Order corresponding to this announcement is 1E1926.
